decisions.reason: As a core-adjacent safety shoe line launched only in 2023, it is still an inexpensive option to keep open while the firm learns about customer uptake through its existing footwear channels.
The comfort insole complements the established footwear business, likely has low continuation cost, and needs more time on the market before its value is fully revealed.
The supportive insole is a close extension of the firm’s core offer, so management would preserve this low-cost option until demand differences versus other insole variants become clearer.
The ergonomic safety shoe series received strong initial prominence and fits the firm’s innovation positioning, so it is worth retaining while market response continues to unfold.

Firefighter and rescue boots address a specialized protective-footwear niche, and a large established manufacturer would typically keep this option open at least another period before judging its long-run potential.
Because the moulded insole was highlighted prominently and is a low-risk complement to the main shoe business, keeping it is consistent with real-options logic.
